comments.body:
The settled Brief is published in the architect wiki at revision d180af4 (page Brief). It freezes the objective, priorities, and the open upstream-layout limitation. Use these semantic definition fields and map them to the HuTian schema: domain name PoemWorld; package/command poemworld; world id prefix pw; roles exactly poet (maker), editor (judge), reader (user); one edge only, poet-editor; artifact poem.md; release gate editor approval of the candidate version. Contracts (the prompt text is normative):
- poet: You receive the world's input and any editor revision request or reader observation. Write or revise exactly one short poem in poem.md, preserving the requested subject and explicit form constraints. Return the artifact for editor review. Do not approve or release it. Treat editor requests as acceptance criteria; do not add features or extra files.
- editor: You receive the original input and the poet's poem.md. Compare the poem to the input, the short-poem requirement, and any explicit form constraints. If it falls short, state the concrete defect and request a revision from poet; do not approve that version. If it meets the brief, approve that exact version. Only your approval can pass the release gate, and you re-evaluate every version.
- reader: You receive each version the world publishes. Read it as a user and report concise observations about clarity, imagery, form, and fit to the input. Send observations to poet and editor for their next decisions. You do not edit, judge, approve, or release.

The graph is a directed poet-editor exchange; reader feedback is delivered to both roles as world observation and does not create a graph edge. The release gate is satisfied only by editor approval of the exact version being released; a revision request blocks release. Keep implementation choices (schema filenames, image build details, prompt transport) to builder, while preserving these fields and semantics. Architect owns organization/contract assets and .forgejo/CODEOWNERS; builder owns package code, registrations, images, install/CI/check wiring; operator owns trial and diagnosis; reviewer owns acceptance. issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
# PoemWorld: a three-role world that writes a short poem

Make a new domain for HuTian: PoemWorld, the smallest world that is still a whole world. From a request it writes a short poem, and the system releases the poem once it is approved.

What to make:

- A domain package `poemworld` (command `poemworld`, world id prefix `pw`) beside the seven domains under `src/`, added the way `DEV.md` says a domain is added: its definition through the `hutian.definitions` entry point, its organization graph in `assets/` in Chinese and English, its system and worker images, and its place in `install.sh`, the CI workflows and the per-domain checks.
- Three roles, one of each category a definition needs: `poet` makes the poem (`poem.md`) from the world's input; `editor` assesses it against the input, asks the poet for changes when it falls short, and approves each version; `reader` uses it: it reads each version the world publishes and says how the poem reads, which the poet and the editor watch. One edge, poet and editor. The release is the poem the editor approved last.
- Keep it small: the roles, their contracts and the release gate make it a world, not features.

Where it goes: one pull request to the private repository `a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian`, base branch `dev`, which holds HuTian's code. Merging it is the maintainer's decision after review.

How to try it: on `trial-machine`, install the version you want accepted in a new directory, build its images there from that version (older images on the machine are not that version), run the repository's regression checks there, and run a fresh PoemWorld world with the input "Write a four-line poem about the first snow." to its release. The trial world's workers are Claude Code with the model `claude-sonnet-5-5` at low effort, signed in with the Claude Code OAuth token that trial-machine's commands get as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_2` (give their provider `auth` `claude-oauth` and `credential_env` `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_2`), with at most 16 executions and 2000 model seconds: a simple task, a cheap worker and a small budget are enough to show the world works. The pull request says what was made and how the trial ended: the trial world's id, its release, and the poem.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
# PoemWorld: a three-role world that writes a short poem

Make a new domain for HuTian: PoemWorld, the smallest world that is still a whole world. From a request it writes a short poem, and the system releases the poem once it is approved.

What to make:

- A domain package `poemworld` (command `poemworld`, world id prefix `pw`) beside the seven domains under `src/`, added the way `DEV.md` says a domain is added: its definition through the `hutian.definitions` entry point, its organization graph in `assets/` in Chinese and English, its system and worker images, and its place in `install.sh`, the CI workflows and the per-domain checks.
- Three roles, one of each category a definition needs: `poet` makes the poem (`poem.md`) from the world's input; `editor` assesses it against the input, asks the poet for changes when it falls short, and approves each version; `reader` uses it: it reads each version the world publishes and says how the poem reads, which the poet and the editor watch. One edge, poet and editor. The release is the poem the editor approved last.
- Keep it small: the roles, their contracts and the release gate make it a world, not features.

Where it goes: one pull request to the private repository `a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian`, base branch `dev`, which holds HuTian's code. Merging it is the maintainer's decision after review.

How to try it: on `trial-machine`, install the version you want accepted in a new directory, build its images there from that version (older images on the machine are not that version), run the repository's regression checks there, and run a fresh PoemWorld world with the input "Write a four-line poem about the first snow." to its release. The trial world's workers are Claude Code with the model `claude-sonnet-5-5` at low effort, signed in with the Claude Code OAuth token that trial-machine's commands get as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_2` (give their provider `auth` `claude-oauth` and `credential_env` `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_2`), with at most 16 executions and 2000 model seconds: a simple task, a cheap worker and a small budget are enough to show the world works. The pull request says what was made and how the trial ended: the trial world's id, its release, and the poem.

This feeds the contract standard and release-gate design; the split waits on this judgement.
issue.title: Architect input: PoemWorld acceptance criteria

comments.author: reviewer
comments.body:
Acceptance criteria for the settled PoemWorld organization:

1. The definition has exactly three roles, one per required category: poet (produces poem.md from the input), editor (assesses against the input, requests poet changes when needed, and approves versions), and reader (reads each published version and reports how it reads). The contracts must make those artifacts and handoffs observable.
2. The graph has exactly one edge, between poet and editor, as the objective requires. Reader feedback is a worker input/watch path described by its contract, not an additional organization edge. The release gate is editor approval: the released artifact is the poem.md from the latest editor-approved version, and no unapproved version can be released.
3. The package and organization must expose the command/world identity and bilingual graph/assets required by the objective; the design must leave ownership clear for entry point, images, installer/CI/per-domain checks, and any kernel change.
4. A release candidate is acceptable only after a fresh trial installs that exact world/result release and builder revision, builds its images from that version, runs all repository regression checks on trial-machine (Docker checks included), and drives the exact input “Write a four-line poem about the first snow.” through checkpoint, stop/resume, and release.
5. Trial evidence must identify the required Claude Code configuration (claude-sonnet-5-5, low effort, claude-oauth with credential_env CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_2, limits 16 executions/2000 model seconds), world id, commands/logs, and the poem, with proof that the editor-approved poem equals the released artifact. Operator’s issue #2 records these evidence obligations and diagnosis of every problem.

I will use these criteria when reviewing release/final; they are derived from objective issue #1 and operator issue #2.
